notes: PIPELINE (from the library spec) Ingestion → Product Forensics locks product identity → Trend Adaptation Director translates the 'Concert-Jumbotron Cameo' consumer trend format into a branded commercial application: shaky phone footage films a giant arena screen; the close-up performer on the screen is the subject, never appearing on a literal stage, ending on a held 'ending fairy' gaze, restaged with the product as the hero or the subject's prized possession → Brand-Fit Filter ensures the adaptation reads as playful Gen-Z, not as an unrelated meme → Nano Banana Pro generates keyframes with product-lock conditioning → Omni Flash 1.1 animates with native audio → Dual Critic checks (a) trend-format fidelity and (b) product/brand identity consistency → Repair on either failure → Caption/hashtag pairing suggested to file correctly next to the live trend → Package.
STAGE 1 — INGESTION Product photo plus the brand tone brief: the brand tone.

STAGE 2 — TREND ADAPTATION DIRECTOR + BRAND-FIT FILTER Translates the 'Concert-Jumbotron Cameo' consumer format into a branded commercial application, then filters it so it reads as the brand tone rather than as an unrelated meme.
STAGE 3 — PRODUCT-LOCKED KEYFRAMES + NATIVE-AUDIO MOTION
STAGE 4 — DUAL CRITIC: TREND FIDELITY + BRAND IDENTITY

M-VT0447_Chocolate_Bar_Box___Conversatio.title: VT0447. Chocolate Bar Box — Conversational Edit-Refinement Loop (#1)
M-VT0447_Chocolate_Bar_Box___Conversatio.summary: BASE STATE Either an uploaded clip of the Chocolate Bar Box or a generated base.
M-VT0447_Chocolate_Bar_Box___Conversatio.pipeline: video-input → reference-image-input → prompt → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → 3× text-gen → video-edit → download

requires.name: Base video — uploaded or previously generated

notes: PIPELINE (from the library spec) Ingestion → Base Generation produces or accepts the starting video → Edit-Request Parser converts each natural-language note ('make the lighting warmer', 'swap the background to a kitchen', 'change the camera to a low angle') into a structured Interactions-API turn → Omni Flash 1.1 applies each edit conversationally, preserving everything not mentioned in that turn → Turn-by-Turn Diff Critic confirms only the requested change occurred (no unintended drift elsewhere in frame) → Repair (re-issue the turn with tighter scoping) on any unintended drift → Final-state Package once the director approves the accumulated edits.
STAGE 1 — BASE STATE Either an uploaded clip of the Chocolate Bar Box or a generated base. Every turn below edits the accumulated state, not the original.
STAGE 2 — EDIT-REQUEST PARSER + SEQUENTIAL TURNS Each natural-language note becomes one scoped Interactions-style turn. Everything not mentioned in a turn must survive that turn untouched.
STAGE 3 — TURN-BY-TURN DIFF CRITIC Confirms only the requested change occurred in each turn — unintended drift anywhere else in frame is the failure this stage exists to catch.

N-042_thirty_second_with_score_and_subs.title: 30s Fully Finished: film, original score, mixed, captioned
N-042_thirty_second_with_score_and_subs.summary: INPUTS Product, character and world references plus the written brief.
N-042_thirty_second_with_score_and_subs.pipeline: reference-image-input → character-input → background-input → prompt → 5× text-gen → 4× video-reference → video-concat → 2× text-gen → lyria-3 → merge-audio-video → text-gen → video-subtitle → download
notes: STAGE 1 — INPUTS Product, character and world references plus the written brief. Leave any input you do not need empty.
STAGE 2 — STRATEGY Turns a loose brief into a hard campaign spine: one job, one tension, one through-line device, locked look.
STAGE 3 — THE 30s SCRIPT Written as one continuous film that happens to be cut at the 10s and 20s marks — that is what makes the three clips join invisibly.
STAGE 4 — 3 x 10s CLIPS One writer and one generator per segment. Each writer reads the whole script and extracts only its own segment, carrying the handoff frame from its neighbour.
ENGINE A/B Same writer, same references, different engine. This is how you compare models — one kind, two model strings.
STAGE 5 — ASSEMBLY 3 clips concatenated in order into the finished 30-second film.
